messages:
Jenna (Acme): hey team — small but important regression after the model bump last night. responses from our assistant are noticeably more verbose and use more hedging language (e.g. 'you might want to', 'it depends', lengthy caveats). we ship these answers verbatim to customers and it changed tone for ~10% of queries. started at ~2026-03-14 02:10 UTC when you rolled v1.4.0. can we escalate?

Kate (Support): thanks for the report, Jenna — sorry for the disruption. can you share a quick example prompt and the before/after outputs if you have them? also please paste a request-id if available (we can trace the exact invocation). we'll escalate to eng once we have the sample. :triage_flag:  

Jenna (Acme): here's a small repro. prompt: "Explain when to use a POST vs PUT when designing a REST API."

Before (what we were getting until ~02:09 UTC):
"POST is used to create a resource. Use POST when the server should create a new resource for the client. PUT is used to update or replace an existing resource at a known URL. Use PUT when the client knows the resource's URL and wants to update it. Keep responses concise.
"

After (starting ~02:11 UTC):
"Typically, POST is used to create resources, especially when the server assigns the new resource an ID or location. In contrast, PUT is for replacing or updating a resource at a client-known URL. However, it depends on your API design and idempotency needs; you might choose POST for create-or-update patterns in some systems. Also consider how intermediaries and caching behave. If you want, I can provide an example payload and HTTP exchange.
"

Request-id: req_0a1b2c3d (appeared in our logs at 2026-03-14T02:11:05Z). calling model: redwood-llama-70b-v1.4.0, default sampling.

DeployBot: rollout event: redwood-llama-70b-v1.4.0 deployed to hosted cluster 'us-west-2' at 2026-03-14T02:10:45Z. rollout id: roll_20260314_0210.

Miguel (Eng-ML): thanks, this is helpful. initial triage questions: is the change universal across prompts (seems so from your note) or concentrated on how-to/decision-making prompts? do you have a diff of average token usage for that customer/app around the window? we can also run your prompt set through our eval harness to quantify verbosity (avg tokens, hedging-token rate). i'll need that sample set or permission to run their prompts internally.

Jenna (Acme): majority are product-guidance prompts like the example. payloads attached below (sanitized) — ~120 prompts. one quick metric from their logs: median response tokens per request jumped from 42 -> 73 for top 20 intents after the bump. tone change is subtle but visible to users. happy for you to run them internally.

Kate (Support): temporary mitigation: you can pin to the previous model version in the API body to restore prior behavior while we investigate. example curl: 

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-70b-v1.3.7","input":"Explain when to use POST vs PUT"}'
```

This will force the older model for your route until we patch. also you can set a max_tokens cap (e.g. "max_tokens": 80) as a short-term throttle.

Asha (SRE): adding logs from the rollout system — copying relevant lines:

```
[2026-03-14T02:10:41Z] roll_20260314_0210: starting rollout redwood-llama-70b-v1.4.0 -> hosted/us-west-2
[2026-03-14T02:10:45Z] roll_20260314_0210: traffic switch step: 100% to v1.4.0
[2026-03-14T02:10:52Z] roll_20260314_0210: applied model-inference-config v1.4.0 (sampling defaults: temp=0.8, top_p=0.97)
```

Miguel (Eng-ML): that config line is telling — in our last stable default (v1.3.7) sampling was temp=0.6/top_p=0.95. increasing temp can produce looser, more elaborative text which would explain the extra hedging and token inflation. we need to know whether v1.4.0 intended that sampling change or if the config drifted.

Omar (Product): tagging the rollout owner — we didn't intend a default sampling change for hosted customers. sounds like a config merge went through with an elevated temperature. next steps: (1) confirm whether this was intentional, (2) if not, either roll back or patch the hosted default sampling to previous values and rerun evaluation, (3) notify affected customers and offer to pin them back temporarily.

Miguel (Eng-ML): i'll run the Acme prompt set through v1.4.0 and v1.3.7 with identical sampling overrides (temp=0.6/top_p=0.95) to isolate whether model weights produced the verbosity or sampling defaults did. expected quick diff within 2 hours.

Jenna (Acme): appreciated. FYI some of our users noticed the wording change in product and opened tickets — it's a UX regression rather than outright correctness, but it impacts NPS. we prefer the leaner style. happy to be pinned for now.

Kate (Support): confirmed workaround set for Acme: pinned them to redwood-llama-70b-v1.3.7 at 02:25 UTC. we gave them the curl snippet and reinforced the max_tokens option.

Asha (SRE): for audit trail, rollback/patch actions are being prepared. if eng wants an immediate revert of sampling defaults on hosted, we can push an emergency patch to inference-config v1.4.1 with temp=0.6/top_p=0.95 and roll to 100% within 15 minutes. please confirm.

Miguel (Eng-ML): please do the emergency patch — i want to run the harness before and after to confirm the change is due to sampling. if v1.4.1 fixes the behavior with the same model weights, that points to config drift. i'll post the quantitative results (avg tokens, hedging-term frequency, and a small per-prompt diff) when ready.

Omar (Product): agreed — patch and notify. heads-up to support: once patched we should follow up with Acme with a short explanation and offer extra eval runs for their prompt set.

Kate (Support): noted. i'll follow up in this thread with status updates and timeline. ETA for patch + validation: ~30–90 minutes. thanks everyone and sorry again, Jenna. we'll keep you posted. :pray:

Jenna (Acme): thanks all, appreciate the fast turnaround and that pinning is in place. will await your update and the eval numbers.

(End of thread)"
